Who is considered the greatest among the Kalyani Chalukyas, credited by Bilhana with building the city of Kalyani and making it his capital?
Which Kakatiya ruler was given control over Hanumakonda by Someswara I in appreciation of his services in the Konkan and Chakrakuta expedition?
In the Kopparam battle of C.E. 1053–54, the Western Chalukyas killed which Chola ruler?
Someswara I ended his life by jumping into which river on 28th March C.E. 1068, after failing to appear for battle and losing the kingdom to Virarajendra?
faqs.e: This followed his defeat in two wars fought at Kudali Sangamam; he is remembered as the ruler who fought incessantly with four emperors.

faqs.q: Someswara II was defeated and had his kingdom occupied by which younger brother, who had been placed in charge of protecting Gangavadi?
Which new era did Vikramaditya VI start in the very first year of his reign, replacing the earlier Salivahana era?
faqs.e: The Chalukya Vikrama era commenced from C.E. 1076.

faqs.q: Which two poets were patronised in the court of Vikramaditya VI?
Someswara III, son of Vikramaditya VI, wrote which encyclopedic work, also called "manasollasam"?
Which minister of Tailapa III, discharging duties as minister, gradually grew stronger and secured the cooperation of feudatory kingdoms?
In which year did Kalachuri Bijjala drive away Tailapa III from Kalyani?
Which Hoyasala ruler defeated Someswara IV (son of Tailapa III) at Kalyani in C.E. 1183, effectively ending the Kalyani Chalukyan dynasty?
faqs.e: Someswara IV lived in exile thereafter and died in C.E. 1200, marking the definitive end of the Kalyani Chalukyan dynasty.

faqs.q:
Consider the following pairs of Kalyani Chalukya rulers and their reign periods:
(I) Tailapa II – 973 – 997 A.D.
(II) Someswara I – 1042 – 1068 A.D.
(III) Vikramaditya VI – 1076 – 1126 A.D.
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
What was the basic nature of Chalukyan government?
Kingly authority in the Chalukyan age consisted of seven items (saptanga). Which of the following is NOT one of them?
faqs.e: The seven items were king, minister, kingdom, treasury, army, friend and fort. Purohit was a separate council-of-ministers member, not one of the seven saptanga items.

faqs.q: What was the crown prince, who assisted the king in administration, also called?

Consider the following statements regarding the Chalukyan council of ministers:
(I) It included the minister, commander-in-chief, treasurer, purohit and yuvaraja.
(II) These posts were held hereditarily and were reserved exclusively for brahmins throughout the Chalukyan period.
(III) During Chalukyan times, these posts were gradually also held by Sudras.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement II is incorrect — though these posts were generally held by trustworthy brahmins initially, they gradually came to be held by Sudras as well.

faqs.q: In the Vemulavadi inscription of Arikesari II, which term refers to employees who perhaps served as department supervisors?

(I) Rashtra (province) – Rashtradhipati

What were the special judges, who resolved disputes between villages over land borders or water use, called?
faqs.e: These courts followed principles recorded in ancient Smriti works such as the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

As per the codes of Saktivarma, followed by the Mudigonda and Vengi Chalukyas, how many drammas were levied as penalty for killing a person?
As per the Srimadhavigeya maharaja inscription of Vaidumba king Bhuvanatrinetra, what punishment was imposed on women in cases of sexual atrocities?
faqs.e: For the same offence, men were fined 64 gadyanas.

faqs.q: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesi II gives details of how many types of army organisations?

Consider the following statements regarding the six types of army organisation described in the Aihole inscription:
(I) "Mula" refers to the hereditary force.
(II) "Atavika" refers to forces of forest-based tribes.
(III) "Amitra" refers to armies of friendly kingdoms.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement III is incorrect — "Amitra" refers to captured forces; armies of friendly kingdoms were called "Mitra."

faqs.q: What were army employees called (meaning "Great Commander-in-Chief") in the Chalukyan age?
Who bore full responsibility for the protection of a fort in the Chalukyan military organisation?
For tax purposes, Chalukyan-age agricultural lands were divided into how many types?
faqs.e: The four types were low-lying/wet lands, dry lands, sandy lands (garuvu) and garden lands.

Feudatories of which Chola ruler dug the Polinayaka and Potta tanks?
What term indicated the extent of tax exemption given when land was donated?

faqs.e: Goods instead came in Chinese ships from Eastern countries and East Indies; Eastern Chalukyas maintained friendly relations with Burma and China via ambassadors.

faqs.e: Statement III is incorrect — Chalukyan-era opportunities to assume feudatory authority extended to sudras as well, as shown by statements I and II.

Who propagated Vira Vaishnavism?
